q.q: A root-filled tooth with a post has a narrow, isolated deep pocket, a recurrent sinus tract and a J-shaped radiolucency along the root. What is the most likely diagnosis?
q.e: An isolated narrow deep pocket with a J-shaped (halo) radiolucency on a root-filled tooth, often with a post, is the classic picture of a vertical root fracture.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q19-F)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q19-F cites: American Association of Endodontists. Diagnostic Criteria for Application in Epidemiological Studies on Root Cracks and Fractures in Root-Filled Teeth; American Association of Endodontists. Endodontic Periodontic Lesions. 2024.
q.n: The candidate said several questions were about vertical root fracture. The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A vertical root fracture is confirmed in a single-rooted, root-filled tooth. What is the management?
q.e: A vertical root fracture in a single-rooted tooth is hopeless, so the tooth is extracted. In a multirooted tooth, the fractured root alone can sometimes be amputated.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q7-O)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q7-O cites: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 12th ed. Vertical-root-fracture diagnosis and management section.
q.n: The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: An impacted lower third molar: the space between the distal of the second molar and the ramus is smaller than the crown's mesiodistal width. What is its Pell and Gregory class?
q.e: Pell and Gregory classify by ramus relationship. Class I has enough space for the whole crown, Class II has less space than the crown width, and in Class III the tooth is entirely within the ramus. Positions A–C describe depth relative to the occlusal plane.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Hupp JR et al. Contemporary Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. Classification of impacted teeth.
q.n: The recall only said "impacted 3rd molar, class?". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: An infant with natal teeth has an ulcer on the ventral surface of the tongue. What is it?
q.e: Riga–Fede disease is a traumatic ulcer on the ventral tongue caused by natal or neonatal teeth rubbing during suckling. It is managed by smoothing the incisal edge or, if needed, removing the tooth.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Riga–Fede disease.
q.n: Recalled as "rede fede". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A patient has clubbing of the fingers. Which investigation should be requested?
q.e: Finger clubbing is most often linked to chronic lung disease (lung cancer, bronchiectasis, fibrosis) or cyanotic heart disease, so a chest X-ray is the first investigation.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Little JW et al. Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. Physical evaluation.

q.q: When is a band-and-loop space maintainer indicated?
o: Loss of a primary second molar before the first permanent molar erupts
Premature loss of a single primary molar on one side
Loss of several primary molars on both sides with erupted incisors
q.e: A band and loop holds space for a single missing primary molar on one side. A lingual arch is used when several teeth are lost on both sides with the permanent incisors erupted. A distal shoe is used when the second primary molar is lost before the first permanent molar erupts.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. Space maintenance.
q.n: The recall only said "band and loop". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A cephalometric ANB angle of 7° indicates which skeletal classification?
q.e: The ANB angle classifies the skeletal pattern: about 2–4° is Class I, more than 4° is Class II, and less than 0–2° (negative) is Class III.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Proffit WR et al. Contemporary Orthodontics. Cephalometric analysis.
q.n: The recall only said "class what? Skeletal". The question was written around the skeletal classification, so check it against what you remember of the exam.

q.q: A patient on stable warfarin needs one simple extraction. The INR taken within 24 hours is below 3.5. What do you do?
o: Stop warfarin for 5 days before extraction
Continue warfarin and extract with local hemostatic measures
q.e: With a stable INR up to 3.5, simple extractions go ahead without stopping warfarin. Use local measures: sutures, a hemostatic dressing and tranexamic acid mouthwash. Stopping warfarin risks thromboembolism.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S10-Q653)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q653 cites: Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness Programme. Management of Dental Patients Taking Anticoagulants or Antiplatelet Drugs. 2nd ed. 2022; Little and Falace's Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. 10th ed. Anticoagulant therapy.
q.n: There were several INR and warfarin questions; one gave an INR below 3.5.

q.q: A patient on warfarin needs an extraction, but the INR is above 4. What do you do?
o: Postpone the extraction and refer to the physician to adjust the INR
Stop warfarin yourself and extract the next day
q.e: Above the safe range (more than about 3.5–4), the extraction is deferred and the physician adjusts the anticoagulation. The dentist never stops or changes warfarin without the prescriber.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q653)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q653 cites: Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness Programme. Management of Dental Patients Taking Anticoagulants or Antiplatelet Drugs. 2nd ed. 2022; Little and Falace's Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. 10th ed. Anticoagulant therapy.
q.n: Another of the INR questions gave an INR above 4.

q.q: A 30-kg child needs ibuprofen at 10 mg/kg per dose. What is the single dose?
q.e: 10 mg/kg × 30 kg = 300 mg, every 6–8 hours. The usual pediatric range is 4–10 mg/kg per dose, which is 120–300 mg for a 30-kg child.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q213)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q213 cites: American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry. Useful Medications for Oral Conditions. Latest revision 2025.
q.n: The recall said "calculate ibuprofen for 30 kg"; the 10 mg/kg dose is the usual one used in these questions.

q.q: Which burs are used to gain endodontic access through a porcelain-fused-to-metal crown?
o: A carbide bur through both porcelain and metal
A diamond bur through the porcelain, then a carbide (transmetal) bur through the metal
A diamond bur through both layers
q.e: Diamonds cut ceramic with less chipping, and carbide (or transmetal) burs cut metal efficiently, so they are used in sequence.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q140)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q140 cites: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 12th ed. Access through existing restorations.
q.n: The recall said "burs used to penetrate crown". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A dentigerous cyst surrounds an impacted tooth that won't be kept. What is the treatment?
o: Enucleation with curettage and removal of the tooth
q.e: Most dentigerous cysts are treated by enucleation (with curettage) and removal of the associated tooth. Marsupialization is reserved for very large cysts, or when the tooth is to be kept and guided into eruption.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S10-Q534)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q534 cites: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. 5th ed. Dentigerous cyst.
q.n: The candidate chose enucleation with curettage.

q.q: A dark-skinned woman has a rapidly appearing pigmented oral lesion; histology shows dendritic melanocytes throughout an acanthotic epithelium. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: Oral melanoacanthoma is a benign, often fast-growing pigmented lesion, most common in young dark-skinned women. It shows acanthosis with dendritic melanocytes and often resolves after biopsy. Acantholysis (loss of cell cohesion) is the hallmark of pemphigus.
q.c: Candidate's answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Check the histology word.
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Oral melanoacanthoma.
q.n: The candidate recalled "acantholysis" and chose melanoacanthoma. The finding for melanoacanthoma is acanthosis, so the stem may have said acanthosis.

q.q: A child has an inflamed distal shoe on one side where the first permanent molar is now erupting; on the other side the first molar has not erupted. What replaces the distal shoe?
o: Reverse band and loop (banded to the erupted first molar)
Leave it and remove the distal shoe without replacement
q.e: Once the first permanent molar has erupted, the distal shoe is no longer needed for guidance. Space is held with a reverse band and loop from the molar to the primary first molar. A lingual arch needs both first molars erupted.
q.c: Candidate's answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. Space maintenance.
q.n: The candidate chose reverse band and loop. The KMZ Pedo file gives the same answer.

q.q: A patient has a moon face. Which test confirms the suspected condition?
q.e: Moon facies points to Cushing syndrome (excess cortisol), which is confirmed by measuring cortisol (e.g., 24-hour urinary free cortisol or a dexamethasone suppression test).
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q12)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q12 cites: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases. Cushing's Syndrome. Clinical features. 2021.

q.q: Where is the middle mesial canal of the mandibular first molar found?
o: Mesial to the mesiobuccal canal, outside the groove
In the groove between the mesiobuccal and mesiolingual canals
q.e: The middle mesial canal lies in the developmental groove between the MB and ML orifices. It is found by troughing that groove under magnification.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Mandibular molar canal anatomy.
q.n: The recall only said "middle mesial canal question". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A slow-growing, painless, firm mass sits in front of the ear. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Warthin tumor of the submandibular gland
q.e: The parotid lies in front of the ear, and pleomorphic adenoma is the most common parotid (and salivary) tumour. Warthin tumour also occurs in the parotid, but not in the submandibular gland.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q379)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q379 cites: WHO Classification of Head and Neck Tumours. 5th ed. Salivary gland tumours.

q.q: How long is a laterally luxated permanent tooth splinted after repositioning?
q.e: IADT guidelines: lateral luxation needs a flexible splint for 4 weeks. Subluxation and extrusion need 2 weeks, and cervical root fractures up to 4 months.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q2)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q2 cites: Hargreaves KM, Cohen S, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 10th ed. Chapter 17, “The Role of Endodontics After Dental Traumatic Injuries,” root-fracture treatment section, pp.621 onward Andreasen JO, Andreasen FM, Andersson L, eds. Textbook and Color Atlas of Traumatic Injuries to the Teeth. 5th ed. Chapter 15, “Root Fractures,” pp.377-412
q.n: The candidate asked how many weeks; the IADT guidelines give 4 weeks.

q.q: An old denture is worn overnight; the palate under it is diffusely red. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: Diffuse erythema limited to the denture-bearing area, with overnight wear and poor hygiene, is denture stomatitis (Candida). It is treated with denture hygiene, removing the denture at night and antifungals.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S06-Q2-C)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S06-Q2-C cites: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. 13th ed. Denture stomatitis and oral candidiasis.
q.n: The recall only said "denture stomatitis". The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A patient needs new dentures but the mucosa is inflamed from the old one. What do you do before the final impression?
o: Treat the tissue first (tissue conditioner or leave the denture out) and take the impression after it heals
Prescribe antibiotics and take the impression the same day
q.e: Impressions of inflamed, distorted tissue give an ill-fitting denture. Rest the tissue first with a temporary tissue conditioner or by leaving the denture out (at least 24 hours), and take the impression once it has recovered.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S06-Q113)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S06-Q113 cites: Zarb GA et al. Prosthodontic Treatment for Edentulous Patients. Tissue conditioning before definitive treatment.
q.n: Recalled as "denture medication and wait to take impression after irritation to mucosa".

q.q: The day after an amalgam restoration, the patient has pain in the TMJ area. What is the cause?
q.e: A high restoration makes the jaw deviate to avoid the contact, which strains the muscles and the TMJ. Check with articulating paper and adjust the occlusion.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S02-Q74)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S02-Q74 cites: Heymann HO, Swift EJ, Ritter AV. Sturdevant's Art and Science of Operative Dentistry.

q.q: What does using warm water when mixing an impression material (e.g., alginate) do?
o: Shortens the working and setting time
q.e: Heat speeds the setting reaction, so warm water shortens working and setting time. Cold water is used to lengthen working time.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Anusavice KJ et al. Phillips' Science of Dental Materials. Alginate setting time.
q.n: Recalled as "impression material increasing time → hot". Heat increases the setting rate (shorter time); cold lengthens it.

q.q: During irrigation, the patient suddenly has severe pain, rapid swelling and bleeding from the canal. What happened?
q.e: Immediate severe pain, rapid swelling, bruising and bleeding into the canal during irrigation is the classic hypochlorite accident.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q6-L)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q6-L cites: Guivarc’h M, et al. Sodium hypochlorite accident: a systematic review. J Endod. 2017;43(1):16-24. doi:10.1016/j.joen.2016.09.023.
q.n: There were 3 questions on sodium hypochlorite accidents. The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: How is a sodium hypochlorite accident managed?
o: Stop irrigating, reassure, cold compresses then warm, analgesics, and antibiotics if infection risk; refer if the airway is affected
Inject more sodium hypochlorite to neutralize it
Continue irrigating to dilute the hypochlorite
q.e: Management is supportive. Stop and irrigate gently with saline, give analgesia, use cold compresses first then warm ones, and prescribe antibiotics if infection risk or tissue necrosis is likely. Reassure the patient and review. Refer urgently if the swelling threatens the airway.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; consistent with Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 hypochlorite questions (S01-Q6-L)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q6-L cites: Guivarc’h M, et al. Sodium hypochlorite accident: a systematic review. J Endod. 2017;43(1):16-24. doi:10.1016/j.joen.2016.09.023.
q.n: The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: How are sodium hypochlorite accidents prevented?
o: A large open-ended needle wedged in the canal
A side-vented needle 1–2 mm short of working length, never bound in the canal, with gentle pressure
Irrigating with high pressure past the apex
q.e: Use a side-vented needle placed loosely, short of working length, moved up and down with light pressure, under rubber dam. Avoid binding and forceful injection, especially with open apices.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Irrigation safety.
q.n: The recall named only the topic; the question and options were written around it.

q.q: A patient on bisphosphonates has asymptomatic exposed bone with no pain or infection. What is the management?
q.e: Stage 1 medication-related osteonecrosis (exposed bone, no symptoms or infection) is managed with an antimicrobial rinse such as chlorhexidine, education and regular review. Antibiotics and debridement are kept for symptomatic or infected stages.
q.c: Candidate's answer; Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q454)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q454 cites: American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons. MRONJ Position Paper—2022 Update.
q.n: The candidate chose "only chlorhexidine mouthwash" for a bisphosphonate patient with no pain.

q.q: A patient has an edge-to-edge anterior bite. The posterior teeth don't occlude in maximum intercuspation but contact during protrusion. What occlusal interference is present?
q.e: Posterior contacts during protrusion, when the anterior teeth should disclude the posteriors, are protrusive interferences.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Rosenstiel SF et al. Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics. Occlusion.

q.q: A child has marks of abuse (bruises and injuries). What type of abuse is it?
q.e: Visible marks such as bruises, burns or injuries in unusual places point to physical abuse. The dentist treats, documents and reports.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry. Oral and Dental Aspects of Child Abuse and Neglect.

q.q: An elderly edentulous woman with ridge resorption and an atrophic tongue complains of a burning tongue. What is the management?
q.e: An atrophic (smooth) burning tongue in an elderly patient suggests a nutritional deficiency such as iron, B12 or folate. Investigate and correct the diet.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. Atrophic glossitis.

q.q: A white lesion on the buccal mucosa with red gingiva keeps recurring despite antivirals. What do you give this time?
q.e: A recurrent white or red lesion that doesn't respond to antivirals is candidiasis, so an antifungal such as fluconazole is used.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. Oral candidiasis.
q.n: Recalled as "Fluconoide (if it is fluconazole, that's the right choice)".

q.q: A patient with active tuberculosis needs emergency dental care. What respiratory protection does the dentist wear?
o: No mask if the patient wears one
q.e: Active TB spreads by airborne droplet nuclei, so a fit-tested N95 (or higher) respirator is needed. Only emergency care is given, ideally in an airborne-isolation room.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: CDC. Guidelines for Infection Control in Dental Health-Care Settings. Tuberculosis.
q.n: Recalled as "infiltrative mask", meaning a filtering (N95) respirator.

q.q: A child has white, hypoplastic-looking spots on the first molars and incisors. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: Demarcated opacities limited to the first permanent molars and incisors are molar–incisor hypomineralization. Fluorosis and amelogenesis imperfecta are generalized.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S02-Q36-B)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S02-Q36-B cites: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. 11th ed. Molar-incisor hypomineralization; Neville BW, et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. 4th ed. Enamel defects.

q.q: Long scenario: a patient has a bald (smooth, depapillated) tongue. Which test is done?
q.e: A depapillated tongue is often candidal (median rhomboid or atrophic candidiasis). A cytology smear quickly confirms Candida hyphae.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Check the scenario details.
q.r: Where to read more: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. Candidiasis and depapillated tongue.

q.q: A child had a palatal ulcer last year that healed within a week; it has come back now, 2 days after measles. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: Recurrence on keratinized palatal mucosa at the same site, triggered by fever or illness, is recurrent intraoral herpes. The first episode was the primary infection.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S03-Q93-C)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S03-Q93-C cites: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. 13th ed. Herpes simplex infection; Neville BW, et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. 4th ed.

q.q: A patient's dentures become loose and no longer fit as the jaw enlarges over time; radiographs show a cotton-wool appearance. What is it?
q.e: Paget's disease causes progressive enlargement of the jaws, so dentures stop fitting, and radiographs show a cotton-wool pattern with hypercementosis.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Paget's disease of bone.
q.n: There were several Paget's questions in this exam. Appears 2× in the recall.

q.q: A dentigerous cyst measures 4 × 3 cm. How is it managed?
o: Enucleation in one stage regardless of size
q.e: Very large cysts are decompressed by marsupialization first, to protect adjacent structures, then the remnant is enucleated. Small cysts are enucleated directly.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S10-Q534)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S10-Q534 cites: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. 5th ed. Dentigerous cyst.
q.n: Recalled answer: marsupialization. Compare with the 2 Nov question on a small dentigerous cyst (enucleation).

q.q: In a patient with bulimia nervosa, which erosion site is most diagnostic?
o: Occlusal surfaces of the mandibular premolars
Palatal surfaces of the maxillary teeth
Buccal surfaces of the mandibular molars
Lingual surfaces of the mandibular incisors
q.e: Vomited acid washes over the palatal surfaces of the upper teeth, while the tongue protects the lower lingual surfaces.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Ritter AV et al. Sturdevant's Art and Science of Operative Dentistry. Erosion.

q.q: A newborn has asymptomatic multiple white nodules on the palatal raphe. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: Epstein pearls are keratin cysts along the midpalatal raphe. They resolve on their own.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Palatal cysts of the newborn.

q.q: The radiograph/diagram shows a mandibular fracture through the tooth-bearing area. How is it classified?
q.e: Fractures through the tooth-bearing part of the mandible open into the mouth through the PDL, so they are compound (open). Antibiotics are usually indicated.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Hupp JR et al. Contemporary Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. Mandibular fractures.

q.q: Which test confirms a bullous (pemphigus or pemphigoid) lesion?
o: Direct immunofluorescence of a perilesional biopsy
q.e: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional tissue shows the antibody pattern: intercellular in pemphigus, linear basement-membrane in pemphigoid.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Vesiculobullous diseases.

q.q: A patient has periorbital ecchymosis after trauma and an orbital fracture is suspected. Which imaging?
q.e: CT (axial and coronal) is the standard imaging for orbital and midface fractures.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Hupp JR et al. Contemporary Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. Midface fractures.

q.q: A cephalogram shows Class II division 1 with a retrognathic mandible, and the adult patient wants surgery. Which procedure?
q.e: A retrognathic mandible is advanced with a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO).
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Proffit WR et al. Contemporary Orthodontics. Orthognathic surgery.

q.q: After a car accident, a patient arrives at the ER with body and dental injuries and difficulty breathing; vital signs are normal. What is the first management?
o: Jaw thrust to open the airway (protecting the cervical spine)
q.e: Airway comes first. In trauma with a possible neck injury, the airway is opened with a jaw thrust, not a head tilt.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: ATLS principles; Malamed SF. Medical Emergencies in the Dental Office.

q.q: A controlled diabetic who had breakfast feels dizzy as he stands up straight after the dentist raised the chair quickly. What is the cause?
o: Orthostatic (postural) hypotension from raising the chair too quickly
q.e: He had eaten and his sugar is controlled. Dizziness on suddenly standing is postural hypotension; raise the chair slowly and let the patient sit for a moment.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Malamed SF. Medical Emergencies in the Dental Office. Postural hypotension.

q.q: A woman on chemotherapy for breast cancer has an asymptomatic cavity. What is done now?
o: No treatment now (defer elective care during chemotherapy)
q.e: During active chemotherapy, elective treatment of an asymptomatic lesion is deferred because of neutropenia and bleeding risk. Prevention is maintained and the tooth is treated once blood counts allow.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Many references would place a temporary restoration if counts allow.
q.r: Where to read more: Little JW et al. Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. Cancer chemotherapy.

q.q: A hemophilia patient has less than 1% factor VIII. What does he have?
q.e: Factor VIII deficiency is hemophilia A, and a level below 1% is severe.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Little JW et al. Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. Bleeding disorders.

q.q: Which syndrome has exophthalmos (with dental anomalies)?
q.e: Crouzon syndrome (craniosynostosis) has shallow orbits with proptosis, midface hypoplasia and dental crowding. Multiple supernumerary teeth are more typical of cleidocranial dysplasia.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ If supernumeraries are the key feature, think cleidocranial dysplasia.
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Craniofacial syndromes.
q.n: Recalled as "syndrome with supernumerary teeth and exophthalmos = Crouzon".

q.q: A white line runs along the buccal mucosa at the level of the occlusal plane. What is it?
q.e: Linea alba is a harmless frictional keratosis along the occlusal line. No treatment is needed.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Linea alba.

q.q: What is the main route of hepatitis B transmission in dentistry?
q.e: HBV spreads mainly through blood and body fluids, for example needlestick injuries.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: CDC. Infection control in dental settings. Bloodborne pathogens.

q.q: A woman who has never had fillers has sudden swelling of the upper lip. What is the most likely diagnosis?
q.e: Sudden, diffuse, painless lip swelling with no injected filler suggests angioedema (allergic or ACE-inhibitor related).
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. Angioedema.

q.q: A new dentist with a history of inactive TB can't take the hepatitis B vaccine because of a medical contraindication. What about his employment?
o: Force him to take the vaccine
Hire him but keep him away from high-risk areas
q.e: A documented contraindication isn't grounds for refusal. He is employed with risk reduction and kept away from high-exposure duties.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: CDC. Immunization of Health-Care Personnel.

q.q: An 8-year-old had an enamel–dentin fracture with pulp exposure 3 days ago; the radiograph is normal and the pulp responds normally. What is the treatment?
q.e: After a delay of days, a vital young pulp with an exposure is treated by partial (Cvek) pulpotomy, removing the inflamed surface pulp.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q166)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q166 cites: American Association of Endodontists. Recommended Guidelines for the Treatment of Traumatic Dental Injuries. 2026. Complicated crown-fracture section.

q.q: How long is a laterally luxated tooth splinted?
q.e: IADT guidelines: lateral luxation is splinted with a flexible splint for 4 weeks.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q2)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q2 cites: Hargreaves KM, Cohen S, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 10th ed. Chapter 17, “The Role of Endodontics After Dental Traumatic Injuries,” root-fracture treatment section, pp.621 onward Andreasen JO, Andreasen FM, Andersson L, eds. Textbook and Color Atlas of Traumatic Injuries to the Teeth. 5th ed. Chapter 15, “Root Fractures,” pp.377-412
q.n: Also asked in the 2 Nov exam.

q.q: An avulsed tooth was out of the mouth for more than 1 hour and is replanted. How long is it splinted?
q.e: IADT guidelines: avulsed and replanted teeth get a flexible splint for 2 weeks, whatever the dry time, or 4 weeks with an alveolar fracture.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q9)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q9 cites: Hargreaves KM, Cohen S, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 10th ed. Chapter 17, “The Role of Endodontics After Dental Traumatic Injuries,” avulsion/splinting section, pp.621 onward Andreasen JO, Andreasen FM, Andersson L, eds. Textbook and Color Atlas of Traumatic Injuries to the Teeth. 5th ed. Chapter 20, “Avulsions,” pp.486-528, and Chapter 39, “Splinting of Traumatized Teeth,” pp.962-971.

q.q: A lower second molar is tender to percussion, doesn't respond to cold and has a sinus tract with a periapical radiolucency; the patient has a bad taste. What is the diagnosis?
o: Pulp necrosis with acute apical abscess
Irreversible pulpitis with symptomatic apical periodontitis
Pulp necrosis with chronic apical abscess
q.e: No response to cold means necrosis. A draining sinus tract with a radiolucency means chronic apical abscess.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: AAE. Glossary of Endodontic Terms. Pulpal and apical diagnoses.

q.q: A patient has pain under a crown whose margin is 1 mm from the bone. Which radiograph best assesses it?
q.e: A vertical bitewing shows the crest-to-margin relation with little distortion. Clinically, bone sounding with a probe confirms biological-width violation.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. The KMZ Fixed file answers periodontal probing (bone sounding) for the same scenario.
q.r: Where to read more: Rosenstiel SF et al. Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics. Biologic width.
q.n: The candidate noted it was "mentioned previously".

q.q: A mother brings her son, saying he has had severe spontaneous pain for 2 weeks; the boy says it started 2 days ago. What is the parent committing?
q.e: Failing to seek care for a known painful condition is dental neglect.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: AAPD. Oral and Dental Aspects of Child Abuse and Neglect.

q.q: A child (cooperative or not) has multiple carious lesions with heavy plaque. Which restoration?
q.e: RMGIC releases fluoride and tolerates moisture, so it suits high-risk children whether cooperative or uncooperative.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. Restorative materials.
q.n: The candidate gave RMGIC for cooperative, uncooperative and heavy-plaque versions of this question. Appears 3× in the recall.

q.q: A girl has scratches on the neck and lesions (petechiae) on the palate. What type of abuse should be suspected?
q.e: Palatal petechiae and bruising, especially with neck marks, should raise suspicion of sexual abuse. Document and report.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: AAPD. Oral and Dental Aspects of Child Abuse and Neglect.
q.n: A second line asked about orofacial abuse with the same answer. Appears 2× in the recall.

q.q: A 9-year-old comes at the end of your clinic with a painful primary molar (pulp involvement). What is done?
q.e: Emergency treatment of a symptomatic vital primary molar with pulp involvement is a pulpotomy.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ The scenario was only partly recalled.
q.r: Where to read more: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. Pulp therapy.
q.n: Recalled as "child 9 yrs came at the end of your clinic → pulpotomy".

q.q: What is the sequence of conventional (Moyers) serial extraction?
o: Primary second molars, then second premolars
Primary laterals, primary canines, primary first molars, then first premolars (BCD4)
First premolars first, then primary canines
q.e: BCD4: primary lateral incisors, then primary canines, then primary first molars, and finally the first premolars.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Proffit WR et al. Contemporary Orthodontics. Serial extraction.

q.q: A mandibular incisor has 4 mm of recession with no loss of interdental bone or soft tissue. What is its 2017 (Cairo) classification?
q.e: RT1 means no interproximal attachment loss, RT2 means interproximal loss up to the buccal loss, and RT3 means interproximal loss greater than the buccal loss.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S03-Q36-B)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S03-Q36-B cites: Newman MG, Takei HH, Klokkevold PR, Carranza FA, eds. Carranza's Clinical Periodontology. 13th ed. Gingival recession; Cairo F. Periodontol 2000. 2017;75:296-316.

q.q: A child has multiple facial caries on the anterior teeth and the mother is concerned about esthetics. Which restoration?
o: Stainless steel crown with resin facing
q.e: An open-face (resin-faced) SSC gives the durability of a crown with an esthetic facial window.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Dean JA, ed. McDonald and Avery's Dentistry for the Child and Adolescent. Anterior crowns.

q.q: A 6-year-old with low caries risk comes for follow-up. Which radiograph?
q.e: Posterior bitewings every 12–24 months are recommended for a low-risk child with closed contacts.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: ADA/FDA. Dental Radiographic Examinations: Recommendations for Patient Selection.

q.q: When you explain the complications of treatment to the patient, which ethical principle are you applying?
q.e: Veracity is the duty to be truthful, including telling the patient the risks and complications.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct. Veracity.

q.q: A shy patient was unhappy with her smile; after the appointment the assistant discussed it with colleagues. Which right was violated (confidentiality is not an option)?
q.e: Discussing a patient's personal concerns with others violates her privacy, and confidentiality is the related duty. The question says confidentiality isn't among the options.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Saudi Commission for Health Specialties. Code of Ethics for Healthcare Practitioners.
q.n: The candidate noted that "confidentiality" wasn't in the options.

q.q: A dentist decides to extract 46 and place an FPD without telling the 75-year-old patient about other options (RCT, implant), believing it's best for him. Which principle is violated?
q.e: Choosing for the patient without presenting the alternatives denies his right to an informed choice (autonomy).
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: ADA Principles of Ethics. Patient autonomy.

q.q: A famous player visits your clinic and you post his photos on social media. What did you break?
q.e: Sharing a patient's identity or images without consent breaches confidentiality.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Saudi Commission for Health Specialties. Code of Ethics.

q.q: The dentist started root canal treatment on 24 instead of 14 by mistake. What should he do?
o: Stop immediately and inform the patient
Finish 24, then do 14 without telling the patient
Ask the assistant to tell the patient later
q.e: Disclose the error at once (veracity), stop and plan care with the patient's informed consent.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: ADA Principles of Ethics. Veracity and disclosure.

q.q: A 14-year-old comes without her parents and asks for a dental "diamond" (cosmetic jewel). What is needed?
q.e: A minor can't consent to elective treatment, so a parent or legal guardian must consent.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Saudi Commission for Health Specialties. Informed consent for minors.

q.q: A patient with Down syndrome comes with a nurse for an extraction under general anesthesia. Who signs the consent?
q.e: If the patient can't give valid consent, the legal guardian (usually the parents) signs, not the accompanying nurse.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Saudi Commission for Health Specialties. Informed consent.

q.q: After a procedure, the dentist washed his hands for 60 seconds and immediately applied alcohol hand rub. What did he do wrong?
o: He should have used hot water
He should have dried his hands before using the alcohol rub (rub on wet hands isn't effective; after washing, it isn't needed)
q.e: Alcohol rub works on dry hands. After a proper soap-and-water wash, hands are simply dried, and alcohol rub straight after on wet hands is wrong.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S09-Q63 cites: World Health Organization. WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care. Handwashing and handrubbing technique.

q.q: A patient has two implants and the distal one is mobile. What do you do?
o: Splint it to the other implant
q.e: A mobile implant has failed to osseointegrate (or lost integration) and must be removed.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Misch CE. Contemporary Implant Dentistry. Implant failure.

q.q: A patient comes 4 months after implant placement with this finding (shown). What is the appropriate management?
q.e: The recall highlights removal. If the finding is only an exposed cover screw with a stable implant, it can be cleaned and left, so check the picture.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Depends on the picture.
q.r: Where to read more: Misch CE. Contemporary Implant Dentistry. Complications.
q.n: The candidate's handwritten note on the picture says the screw is showing.

q.q: The patient moves the mandible to the left. Which side is the working side?
q.e: The side the mandible moves toward is the working side; the opposite side is the non-working (balancing) side.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Rosenstiel SF et al. Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics. Mandibular movements.
q.n: The recall listed the options without a marked answer (two options said "right non-working").

q.q: Sudden bleeding appears during cleaning and shaping. What is most likely?
o: Normal pulp bleeding at the apex
q.e: Sudden persistent bleeding inside a prepared canal, especially away from working length, suggests a perforation. Confirm with an apex locator or radiograph.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Procedural errors.

q.q: How do you negotiate a curved canal?
o: With Gates-Glidden drills to the apex
q.e: Small precurved flexible files (or NiTi) follow the curvature without ledging or transporting the canal.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Curved canals.

q.q: Which obturation technique suits internal resorption?
q.e: Thermoplasticized gutta-percha flows into the irregular resorptive defect.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Internal resorption.

q.q: A child has generalized brownish-yellow translucent enamel, severe attrition and a mother with the same defect. What is the diagnosis?
q.e: A generalized inherited enamel defect affecting all teeth, with a family history, is amelogenesis imperfecta.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Amelogenesis imperfecta.

q.q: A 14-year-old girl has maxillary protrusion (proclined incisors with increased overjet). What is the malocclusion?
q.e: Proclined upper incisors with a large overjet is Class II division 1. Division 2 has retroclined incisors.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Proffit WR et al. Contemporary Orthodontics. Angle classification.

q.q: A child fell and a tooth appears shorter. What injury is this?
q.e: A tooth pushed into the bone looks shorter and is usually immobile with a metallic percussion sound.
q.c: Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q48-A)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q48-A cites: Sigurdsson A, et al. Recommended Guidelines of the American Association of Endodontists for the Treatment of Traumatic Dental Injuries. J Endod. 2026;52(8):1237-1253. doi:10.1016/j.joen.2026.04.002.

q.q: How is a supracrestal (coronal) perforation managed?
o: Seal it immediately (e.g., with GIC or composite)
Seal it with MTA only after 6 months
q.e: A perforation above the bone crest is sealed at once from the outside with a restorative material such as GIC or composite. Subcrestal perforations are repaired with MTA.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Perforation repair.

q.q: What is a barbed broach used for?
q.e: The barbed broach engages and removes pulp tissue (extirpation). It doesn't cut dentin.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Instruments.

q.q: Where is the MB2 canal of the maxillary first molar?
q.e: MB2 lies on the line from MB1 to the palatal canal, about 1–3 mm palatal (mesiopalatal) to MB1.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Maxillary molar anatomy.

q.q: At a routine visit the patient says she has trouble breathing, sleeps on extra pillows, gets tired and has swollen legs. What is it?
q.e: Dyspnea, orthopnea (pillows), fatigue and ankle edema are classic congestive heart failure. Seat the patient upright.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Little JW et al. Dental Management of the Medically Compromised Patient. Heart failure.

q.q: Which impression material has the highest stiffness?
q.e: Polyether is the stiffest elastomer, which makes removal from undercuts harder.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Anusavice KJ et al. Phillips' Science of Dental Materials. Elastomers.

q.q: What is the diameter at D9 of a size 30 file with a 0.04 taper?
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q67)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q67 cites: Hargreaves KM, Cohen S, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 10th ed. Chapter 8, standardized endodontic instruments, pp.223282. Chandra BS, Gopikrishna V, eds. Grossman’s Endodontic Practice. 13th ed. Chapter on instrument standardization and taper; exact pages require verification.

q.q: A parent refuses an indicated extraction for the child. What do you do?
o: Explain again the importance and risks, and document
q.e: Re-explain the need and the risks of no treatment, allow an informed decision, and document the refusal.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: AAPD. Informed consent.

q.q: A tooth has abnormal (increased) mobility after trauma but no displacement. What injury is this?
q.e: Increased mobility without displacement is a subluxation. Tenderness with no increased mobility is a concussion. A lateral luxation is displaced, often locked.
q.c: Corrected after checking; consistent with IADT definitions
q.r: Where to read more: Bourguignon C et al. IADT Guidelines: Fractures and Luxations of Permanent Teeth.
q.n: The candidate recalled "trauma without displacement and abnormal mobility → lateral luxation". A lateral luxation is by definition displaced, so the answer was corrected to subluxation.

q.q: Which CBCT plane best detects a vertical root fracture?
q.e: Axial slices cross the root perpendicular to its long axis, showing the fracture line or the bone loss pattern around it.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Patel S et al. Vertical root fractures in root-filled teeth. Int Endod J.

q.q: What are the abutments shown (a plastic castable sleeve on a metal base)?
q.e: A UCLA abutment is a castable plastic sleeve, sometimes with a machined metal base, used to make a custom cast abutment.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Misch CE. Contemporary Implant Dentistry. Abutments.
q.n: The recall showed only the picture labelled "UCLA abutment".

q.q: Which instrument grasp is shown?
q.e: In the modified pen grasp, the pad of the middle finger rests on the shank, giving control and tactile sense. It is the grasp for periodontal instruments.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Nield-Gehrig JS. Fundamentals of Periodontal Instrumentation.
q.n: The recall showed only the picture labelled "modified pen grasp".

q.q: A patient has an edge-to-edge anterior bite. The posterior teeth don't occlude in maximum intercuspation but contact during protrusion. What interference is present?
q.e: Posterior contacts during protrusion are protrusive interferences.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Rosenstiel SF et al. Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics. Occlusion.
q.n: Also asked in the 2 Nov exam.

q.q: A newly erupted premolar shows an occlusal projection (dens evaginatus, shown). What is the appropriate management?
o: Protect it (sealant or composite) or reduce it gradually
q.e: The tubercle has a pulp horn and fractures easily. It is protected with sealant or composite, or reduced gradually with dentin protection.
q.c: Corrected after checking; consistent with the October bank (OCT-22, OCT10-37)
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Dens evaginatus.
q.n: The candidate chose "follow up". The other banks (October, Deema, KMZ) all give protection or grinding, so the answer was corrected.

q.q: Teeth in only one quadrant are affected ("ghost teeth" with thin enamel and dentin). What is it?
q.e: Regional odontodysplasia affects a localized group of teeth, usually in one quadrant. They look like ghost teeth on radiographs.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Regional odontodysplasia.

q.q: Which bone lesion's pain is characteristically relieved by aspirin?
q.e: Osteoid osteoma causes night pain that is relieved by aspirin or NSAIDs.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Neville BW et al. Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology. Osteoid osteoma.

q.q: Infection from which tooth most commonly spreads to cause cavernous sinus thrombosis (shown)?
o: Maxillary third molar via the buccal space only
q.e: Infection from the maxillary canine (and anterior maxilla) spreads through the valveless angular and ophthalmic veins to the cavernous sinus.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Hupp JR et al. Contemporary Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. Fascial space infections.
q.n: Recalled as "cavernous sinus thrombosis → canine" with the patient photo.

q.q: Why are tetracycline fibers used in periodontal treatment?
o: To keep a high local tetracycline concentration in the pocket (removed after about 10 days)
q.e: Tetracycline fibers are packed into the pocket to release the drug locally at a sustained high concentration. They are an adjunct to scaling and are removed after about 10 days.
q.c: Answer worked out by reasoning; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Newman MG et al. Newman and Carranza's Clinical Periodontology. Local drug delivery.
q.n: The recall showed the question with a picture of the notes, without an answer.

q.q: A lower molar doesn't respond to cold and has a Grade III furcation and mobility. What is the management?
q.e: A non-vital molar with through-and-through furcation involvement and mobility has a hopeless prognosis.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Newman MG et al. Newman and Carranza's Clinical Periodontology. Prognosis.

q.q: Which burs are used for access through a crown?
o: Carbide for metal; diamond for porcelain
Diamond for metal; carbide for porcelain
q.e: Diamonds cut ceramic with less chipping, and carbide or transmetal burs cut metal.
q.c: Confirmed: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 gives the same answer (S01-Q140)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q140 cites: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen’s Pathways of the Pulp. 12th ed. Access through existing restorations.
q.n: Also asked in the 2 Nov exam.

q.q: What is the minimum distance between a natural tooth and an implant?
q.e: At least 1.5 mm between implant and tooth, and 3 mm between two implants, preserves bone and papilla.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Misch CE. Contemporary Implant Dentistry. Implant spacing.

q.q: What is the minimum distance between two adjacent implants?
q.e: At least 3 mm between implants preserves the interimplant bone crest and papilla (Tarnow).
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Tarnow DP et al. J Periodontol. 2000;71:546-549.

q.q: A midline diastema is associated with a high labial frenum. What is the treatment sequence?
q.e: Close the space orthodontically first; the frenectomy follows, so the scar tissue helps retain the closure.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Proffit WR et al. Contemporary Orthodontics. Diastema.

q.q: A patient with Sjögren's syndrome and GERD has good periodontal health but active root caries on many teeth. What is the most immediate step?
o: Refer to a gastroenterologist to control the GERD
q.e: The acid reflux is driving the breakdown alongside the dry mouth, so controlling it comes first. Start intensive fluoride (5,000 ppm toothpaste or varnish) and saliva substitutes at the same time.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Many keys would say high-fluoride therapy is the most immediate preventive step.
q.r: Where to read more: Glick M, ed. Burket's Oral Medicine. Sjögren syndrome.

q.q: A ledge forms during cleaning and shaping. How do you bypass it?
o: Pre-curve a small file (size 8 or 10) and negotiate past the ledge
q.e: A small precurved file, rotated gently with the tip pointing away from the ledge, finds the original canal path.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Ledges.

q.q: A patient has a draining sinus tract on the buccal mucosa. How do you find the offending tooth?
o: Extract the tooth closest to the sinus
Thread a size 20–30 gutta-percha cone into the tract and take a radiograph
q.e: Tracing the sinus with a gutta-percha cone on a radiograph shows which root it leads to.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. Diagnosis.

q.q: A traumatized, root-filled tooth may have a vertical root fracture. What is the most definitive way to confirm it?
q.e: Direct visualization of the fracture line through an exploratory flap is definitive; imaging is only suggestive.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16
q.r: Where to read more: AAE. Cracking the Cracked Tooth Code.

q.q: A periodontal abscess between 21 and 22; both teeth are vital, 22 is tender to percussion and there is localized bone loss. What is the most likely predisposing factor?
q.e: A palatogingival groove on a vital maxillary lateral incisor channels plaque down the root, causing a narrow deep pocket and localized bone loss.
q.c: Corrected after checking; Consistent with a related Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 question (S01-Q19-G)
q.r: Rafi' Al-Maqam 16 S01-Q19-G cites: American Association of Endodontists. Endodontic Periodontic Lesions. 2024; Berman LH, Hargreaves KM, eds. Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp. 12th ed. Endodontic-periodontal interrelationships.
q.n: The candidate chose dens invaginatus. That usually leads to pulp necrosis and an endodontic lesion, but here both pulps are vital and the problem is periodontal, so the answer was corrected.

q.q: Sodium hypochlorite is used in which chemomechanical procedure?
q.e: Chemomechanical caries-removal gels (e.g., Carisolv) are based on sodium hypochlorite, which dissolves the degraded collagen of infected dentin.
q.c: Recalled answer; Not covered in Rafi' Al-Maqam 16. ⚠ Its main use is as a root canal irrigant.
q.r: Where to read more: Ritter AV et al. Sturdevant's Art and Science of Operative Dentistry. Caries removal.
q.n: Recalled as "sodium hypochlorite used for? = caries removal".

q.q: A tooth with no caries or pain is sensitive to percussion; the radiograph shows a well-circumscribed radiopacity at the apex (shown). What is the diagnosis?

q.e: Le Fort I is a horizontal fracture above the teeth. Le Fort II is pyramidal (through the nasal bones and infraorbital rims), and Le Fort III is craniofacial separation.

q.q: How is medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) defined?
o: Exposed or probeable bone in the jaw for more than 8 weeks, with antiresorptive or antiangiogenic drug history and no jaw radiation
Bone necrosis caused by head and neck radiotherapy
Any bone exposure after extraction for 1 week
q.e: MRONJ (AAOMS) is exposed bone, or bone that can be probed through a fistula, persisting more than 8 weeks in a patient with current or past antiresorptive or antiangiogenic therapy and no history of jaw radiation or metastatic disease. Radiation-induced necrosis is osteoradionecrosis.

q.q: A patient has a painless reciprocal click on both opening and closing with a normal range of motion. What is the TMJ diagnosis?
q.e: A reciprocal click (on opening as the disc reduces, and on closing as it displaces again) with normal opening is disc displacement with reduction. A closed lock with limited opening is disc displacement without reduction.

q.q: The lower lip vermilion is atrophic, smooth and blurred at the border (in a sun-exposed patient). What is the treatment?
o: No treatment; it is normal ageing
Sun protection, biopsy of suspicious areas, and vermilionectomy or topical field therapy (e.g., 5-fluorouracil)
q.e: An atrophic lower vermilion with a blurred vermilion–skin border is actinic cheilitis, a potentially malignant condition. Manage it with sun protection, biopsy of any ulcerated, thickened or suspicious area, and vermilionectomy or field therapy (5-FU, imiquimod, laser) for dysplasia.

q.e: Platelet problems cause immediate bleeding and clotting-factor problems cause delayed bleeding. Von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion and carries factor VIII, so von Willebrand disease causes both.

q.e: Mutans streptococci pass mainly from mother to infant through saliva (tasting food, shared spoons), usually during the "window of infectivity".

q.q: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve is already taking amoxicillin, prescribed by another doctor for an infection, and needs an extraction. What about endocarditis prophylaxis?
o: Use an antibiotic from a different class (e.g., azithromycin) for prophylaxis, or delay until 10 days after the course ends
No prophylaxis is needed because he is on amoxicillin
Give the usual 2 g amoxicillin on top
q.e: If a patient is already on an antibiotic, oral streptococci may be resistant to it. AHA guidance is to choose a drug from a different class (azithromycin, clarithromycin or doxycycline; clindamycin is no longer recommended) or wait about 10 days after the current course.

q.q: A surgeon did a coronectomy on a deeply impacted lower third molar and left the roots. Apart from protecting the nerve, what is the reason?
o: The roots are in intimate contact with the inferior alveolar canal (high-risk radiographic signs)
Coronectomy is done for every impacted tooth
The roots were infected and mobile
q.e: Coronectomy is chosen when radiographs show the roots in close relation to the inferior alveolar canal (darkened roots, interrupted canal lines). The vital, immobile roots are left. Infected or mobile roots contraindicate it.

q.q: What is the effect of bisphosphonates on orthodontic treatment?
q.e: Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts, so bone remodeling and tooth movement slow down. Space closure may be incomplete, and the MRONJ risk must also be considered.
